title: Mobile Journey Contract v1
description: WBS-30.01. A domain contract layered ON the shared outcome-contract-v1, never a second lifecycle: this record names no state, history, receipts or decision of its own. outcome_contract_ref points at the real outcome-contract-v1 JSON that owns those (state machine, receipts, history); scripts/mobile_journey_contract.py enforces that the referenced file exists and actually validates as outcome-contract-v1 before this record is accepted, so a journey contract can never point at nothing or at something malformed. Feeds Context Capsule, the unit plan, native evidence obligations (scripts/native_evidence.py, wrapped for Evidence v2 per WBS-30.05, not yet built), and the Journey Passport (WBS-30.06, not yet built). Only the keyword subset scripts/mobile_journey_contract.py actually enforces is used here: type, required, properties, enum, const, items, minItems, additionalProperties -- the same enforced subset outcome-contract-v1 documents, for the same reason (a reader of either file finds the same account).

schema_version.description: Which shape this record follows, so a reader never has to guess.

journey_id.description: A stable identifier for this one bounded journey (WBS-30.10's own rule: one journey, not the most complex feature).

outcome_contract_ref.description: Path to the outcome-contract-v1 record this journey is layered on. Must resolve to a file that exists and validates as outcome-contract-v1 (enforced by hand, since the keyword subset has no cross-file reference check, matching how receipts[].ref is enforced by hand in the shared contract).

human_outcome.description: The outcome a real user experiences when this journey succeeds, in plain words, not an implementation description.

entry_state.description: The app/user state this journey starts from.

exit_state.description: The app/user state this journey ends in when it succeeds.

supported_device_classes.description: Which device classes this journey is claimed to work on. WBS-30.07's Device Matrix names the dimension; this contract states the claim, the matrix proves or refuses it.

supported_os_range.description: The OS version range this journey is claimed to work on, e.g. an iOS range string.

locales.description: Which locales this journey is claimed to work correctly in.

accessibility_obligations.description: What this journey must do for accessibility. May be empty (enforced by hand: an empty array here is a stated decision that none apply, never a silently-skipped field, distinct from the key being absent, which the required list already forbids).

network_state_obligations.description: What this journey must do under named network conditions (offline, slow, interrupted mid-request). May be empty for the same reason as accessibility_obligations.

interruption_obligations.description: What this journey must do when interrupted (backgrounded, a call, a notification). May be empty for the same reason as accessibility_obligations.

privacy_constraints.description: What this journey must never do with user data. May be empty only when the journey genuinely touches no user data (enforced by hand: contract_check-style, an empty array is refused unless human_outcome or entry_state/exit_state names no personal data path).

performance_budgets.description: Named performance budgets this journey must stay inside (e.g. time to first frame, memory ceiling). May be empty.

visual_reference_ids.description: Stable reference IDs into the current mobile_design boards/briefs (WBS-30.03's own reference IDs), not raw asset paths. May be empty for a journey with no visual reference yet.

required_native_tests.description: The exact native test identifiers that must pass for this journey (feeds native evidence obligations, WBS-30.05). At least one: a journey contract with zero required tests cannot ever reach a PASS Journey Passport.

human_acceptance_items.description: What a human must observe and accept for this journey, since a native test suite cannot certify feel or visual correctness on its own. May be empty only for a journey with no human-observable surface.

post_release_claims.description: Claim IDs this journey will feed once released (BrotherDS claims per WBS-30.11: completion rate, crash-free sessions, latency, return usage, helpfulness). Mobile does not score them itself. May be empty before release.
